recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-32446. If FHIR-32445 is reconciled separately, review its broader DICOM mapping request there; the seed itself is satisfied by the removal of the old minor/serious outcome code definitions.
issue_request: FHIR-32446 was Published/Persuasive for R5 after objecting that the AuditEvent outcome definitions for minor and serious failure were tautological and that the HTTP examples did not actually distinguish minor from serious. Its final resolution says it was resolved with FHIR-32445.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-32446-tagged source commit was found. Commit 04aebbe0d4, tagged for FHIR-32445, removed the old AuditEvent outcome codes 4 Minor failure, 8 Serious failure, and 12 Major failure from core AuditEvent outcome source and changed the value set to use issue-severity. Later FHIR-39622 work added success to issue-severity and removed the remaining separate AuditEvent success-code include.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps auditevent=AuditEvent, so the inspected AuditEvent StructureDefinition and outcome value set are current build inputs. The current value set composes http://hl7.org/fhir/issue-severity, whose definitions distinguish success, warning, error, fatal, and information without using the old minor/serious labels. The combined branch already contains the related FHIR-32447 reconciliation for the AuditEvent.outcome backbone and required code binding.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the active current source has already replaced the problematic definitions through the linked FHIR-32445 and later FHIR-39622 terminology changes.
